_meta: Frozen from alp-sdk's scripts/alp_cli/faultdecode.py (bit tables + a swept sample of decode()/report_to_json()/render_human() outputs). Guards tan/core/faultdecode.py's register-level fidelity without needing a live alp-sdk checkout on disk -- see tests/core/test_faultdecode.py. NO LONGER a pure alp-sdk recording: two decode_cases (cfsr 0x20 MLSPERR, cfsr 0x2000 LSPERR) were re-recorded from tan's own decode for tan-cli#616, which deliberately diverges from upstream on root_cause alone. Read faultdecode_golden.PROVENANCE.txt beside this file before changing any value here, and do not hand-edit one to make a test pass.
bit_tables: Instruction access violation -- the MPU blocked an instruction fetch (executing from a no-execute / unprivileged region).
Data access violation -- the MPU blocked a load/store; MMFAR holds the address.
MemManage fault unstacking on exception return -- the exception frame sits in MPU-protected memory (often a corrupted/overflowed stack).
MemManage fault stacking on exception entry -- the stack pointer points into MPU-protected/invalid memory (a bad or overflowed stack).
MemManage fault during lazy floating-point state preservation.
MMFAR holds a valid faulting data address (see below).
Instruction bus error -- a prefetch faulted, usually a branch/call through a bad function pointer into unmapped memory.
Precise data bus error -- a load/store faulted and BFAR holds the exact faulting address (commonly an unclocked/absent peripheral or a bad pointer).
Imprecise data bus error -- a buffered/late write faulted; the PC has moved on, so BFAR is not reliable (look for an earlier bad store).
Bus fault unstacking on exception return -- a corrupted stack pointer.
Bus fault stacking on exception entry -- a bad or overflowed stack pointer.
Bus fault during lazy floating-point state preservation.
BFAR holds a valid faulting data address (see below).
Undefined instruction -- executed a bad/corrupted opcode (often a wild PC or jumping into data).
Invalid state -- EPSR.T cleared or illegal IT state, classically a function pointer called without the Thumb bit (bit 0) set.
Invalid PC on exception return -- a bad EXC_RETURN or a corrupted stacked PC.
No coprocessor -- access to a disabled/absent coprocessor, most often the FPU used before CPACR enables it.
Stack overflow -- the hardware stack-limit (PSPLIM/MSPLIM) tripped (ARMv8-M).
Unaligned access -- an unaligned load/store while alignment trapping is on (or an LDM/STM/LDRD that must be aligned).
Divide by zero -- SDIV/UDIV by zero with DIV_0_TRP enabled.
Vector-table read fault -- a bus error reading an exception vector.
Forced HardFault -- a configurable fault (MemManage/BusFault/UsageFault) was escalated; the real cause is in CFSR above.
Debug event -- a breakpoint/watchpoint fired with no debugger attached.
Breakpoint -- a BKPT instruction or hardware breakpoint.
